explanations: The modern rules emerged in Europe at the end of the 15th century and were universally accepted by the end of the 19th.
Its recorded history begins with chaturanga in 7th-century India; it reached Persia, then the Arab world, then Europe.
In 1997 Deep Blue became the first computer to win a match against a reigning World Champion, defeating Garry Kasparov.
Each player controls sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights and eight pawns.
It is a board game for two players on 64 squares in an 8×8 grid, and the object is to checkmate the enemy king.

sources.excerpt: The modern rules of chess emerged in Europe at the end of the 15th century, becoming standardized and gaining universal acceptance by the end of the 19th century.
The recorded history of chess dates back to the emergence of chaturanga in 7th-century India.
After its introduction to Persia, it spread to the Arab world and then to Europe.
In 1997, Deep Blue became the first computer to win a match against a reigning World Champion when it defeated Garry Kasparov.

The players, referred to as "White" and "Black", each control sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns, with each piece type having a different pattern of movement.
Chess is a board game for two players, played on a square board consisting of 64 squares arranged in an 8×8 grid.
The objective of the game is to checkmate (threaten with inescapable capture) the enemy king.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: xiangqi, janggi and shogi share the same ancestor but are played on different boards and are named in the article as relatives; draughts uses a 64-square board but has one kind of piece and no king to trap.
